speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To begin our evaluation, how long has this pain been present, and did it start after a specific injury or incident?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the mechanism of injury involving a finger caught in a jersey suggests a potential ligament tear or fracture. Did you hear a "pop" at the time of injury, and is the pain and swelling most severe at the base of the finger or more distal?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (extensor tendon rupture of the distal phalanx).

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
